source.method: The runner's own per-assembly duration, from the 'Test run summary' block of each project's step in the shard job log. Harbor.E2E.App.Avalonia is the one exception: it runs as one process per shard (tools/run-e2e-avalonia-shards.py), so its cost is the CRITICAL PATH of those processes, which is what the plan's own report prints (14.7 s of 12.1 / 14.7 / 4.7 s).
source.note: The shard WALLS of the same run, for the reader who wants the raw numbers: core 143 s, ui 62 s, platform 35 s, e2e 24 s. The gate computes the walls from the costs below plus the overhead model; the difference between a computed wall and a measured one is the model.

overhead.note: What a shard spends on the projects rather than in them: the process start and the TRX write, measured at 0.56-0.66 s per project in all four shards of run 39504714459, plus the first project's JIT warm-up (0.6-6.5 s, depending on the project), carried here as a per-shard constant. The constant is the middle of the measured range, not the worst case: a wall predicted from a measurement is an estimate, and the gate compares estimates with each other.
